title: Priming (Behavioral Nudges)
hook: A button in the right spot sells more than a paragraph of persuasion.
statement: Small, well-placed cues trigger action, for your customers and for you.
explainer: A cue only works if people notice it and the action is easy right there. A bold prompt pointing at a clunky checkout still loses the sale.
sop: Name the exact action you want someone to take.
Brainstorm cues that make it more visible: a word, an object, a placement.
Score each cue's Salience and Ease from 1 to 10.
Put the strongest cue right where the action should happen.
Measure whether the action rate actually changed.
equation_example: Salience 7, Ease 8. 7 × 8 = 56. Higher means the cue reliably gets people moving. Lower means it's too subtle to notice, or the action is still too hard once they do.
question: Pick one action you want customers to take and write the cue you'll put in their path.
closing_statement: A visible, easy cue beats a persuasive paragraph.
caption:
Principle Nº 222: Priming (Behavioral Nudges)

A button in the right spot sells more than a paragraph of persuasion.

Small, well-placed cues trigger action, for your customers and for you.

Your turn: Pick one action you want customers to take and write the cue you'll put in their path.
